question: Hoysala is a 30-year brand. Is Hoysala Orchid Springs safe?

result.text:
**Caution: Hoysala Orchid Springs has medium graph risk (42.7/100, CAUTION). The risk sits mainly with its contractor, not the developer.**

- **Contractor record:** Monsoon Infra Contractors, the project's contractor, delivered Chalukya Pearl Residency 26 months late, Mallige Sunrise Heights 22 months late and Lakeshore Tranquil Bay 18 months late. Its on-time share is 0%.
- **Court case:** C.C. 3381/2025, a cheque-bounce case at the Bengaluru Magistrate Court filed in 2025, is listed as pending against Monsoon Infra.
- **Developer group:** Hoysala Yelahanka Projects Pvt Ltd shows no failed companies, stalled projects or court cases. The land (Sy. No. 36/6, Hagadur, A-khata) shows no title issues. Approvals (BBMP plan, RERA, CC) are granted.
- **"30-year brand":** The graph records the Hoysala Living brand from 1996. The developing company was incorporated in 2022, so the age claim applies to the group, not this entity.

**Next step:** Before paying anything, ask the builder for the status of the cheque-bounce case, whether the agreement has delay penalties and a contractor-change clause, and which RERA number applies, since the brochure and approvals list differ. I can also search for alternatives once you share your budget, BHK and preferred localities.

events.name: search_projects
cypher: CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes('Project', 'Hoysala* Orchid* Springs*') YIELD node RETURN node.id AS id LIMIT 10

MATCH (p:Project)<-[:DEVELOPS]-(c:Company)
OPTIONAL MATCH (g:Group)-[:CONTROLS]->(c)
WITH p, c, g
WHERE ($locality IS NULL OR toLower(p.locality) CONTAINS toLower($locality))
  AND ($budget IS NULL OR p.price_min_lakh <= $budget)
  AND ($bhk IS NULL OR $bhk IN p.bhk)
  AND ($ids IS NULL OR p.id IN $ids)
  AND ($include_stalled OR p.status <> 'stalled')
RETURN p.id AS id, p.name AS name, p.locality AS locality, p.status AS status, p.bhk AS bhk,
       p.price_min_lakh AS price_min_lakh, p.price_max_lakh AS price_max_lakh,
       p.launch_year AS launch_year, c.name AS company, g.name AS brand
ORDER BY p.price_min_lakh
LIMIT $limit

cypher:
MATCH (p:Project {id: $id})<-[:DEVELOPS]-(c:Company)
OPTIONAL MATCH (g:Group)-[:CONTROLS]->(c)
OPTIONAL MATCH (d:Person)-[dir:DIRECTOR_OF]->(c)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:BUILT_ON]->(l:LandParcel)
OPTIONAL MATCH (con:Contractor)-[:BUILDS]->(p)
OPTIONAL MATCH (len:Lender)-[:FINANCES]->(p)
RETURN p {.*} AS project, c.name AS company, c.status AS company_status, c.incorporated AS incorporated,
       g.name AS brand, g.brand_since AS brand_since,
       collect(DISTINCT d.name) AS directors, l.name AS land, l.khata AS khata, l.acres AS acres,
       con.name AS contractor, len.name AS lender

MATCH (p:Project {id: $id})-[:HAS_APPROVAL]->(a:Approval)
RETURN a.type AS type, a.status AS status, a.year AS year, a.ref AS ref ORDER BY a.year

MATCH (p:Project {id: $id})<-[:AGAINST]-(c:Complaint)
RETURN c.status AS status, c.category AS category, count(c) AS n

output.how_to_read: risk_score 0-100 = 100*(1-exp(-K)); K sums severity * 0.6^(hops-1) * edge weights over every path to a red flag within 4 hops. share_pct = share of K from that flag; n_paths = how many distinct paths reach it.

cypher:
MATCH path = (p:Project {id: $id})-[:DEVELOPS|DIRECTOR_OF|CONTROLS|BUILT_ON|PREVIOUSLY_OWNED_BY|INVOLVES|AGAINST|HAS_APPROVAL|BUILDS*1..4]-(f:RedFlag)
WHERE f <> p
  AND none(n IN nodes(path)[1..-1] WHERE n.kind = 'Project')
  AND size([r IN relationships(path) WHERE type(r) = 'PREVIOUSLY_OWNED_BY']) <= 1
RETURN f.id AS flag_id, f.kind AS flag_kind, f.name AS flag_name, f.reason AS reason,
       f.severity AS severity, f.created_at AS created_at, length(path) AS hops,
       [n IN nodes(path) | {id: n.id, kind: n.kind, name: n.name}] AS nodes,
       [r IN relationships(path) | type(r)] AS rels
LIMIT 2001

events.name: developer_network
cypher:
CALL algo.WCC({nodeLabels: ['Person', 'Company'], relationshipTypes: ['DIRECTOR_OF']})
YIELD node, componentId
RETURN node.id AS id, componentId AS component

MATCH (c:Company) WHERE c.id IN $company_ids
OPTIONAL MATCH (g:Group)-[:CONTROLS]->(c)
OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[:DEVELOPS]->(p:Project)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)<-[:AGAINST]-(cp:Complaint {status: 'open'})
WITH c, g, p, count(cp) AS open_complaints
RETURN c.id AS company_id, c.name AS company, c.status AS company_status, g.name AS brand,
       collect(CASE WHEN p IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE {id: p.id, name: p.name, status: p.status,
               delay_months: p.delay_months, open_complaints: open_complaints} END) AS projects

MATCH (d:Person)-[r:DIRECTOR_OF]->(c:Company)
WHERE c.id IN $company_ids
RETURN d.id AS person_id, d.name AS person, c.id AS company_id, c.name AS company,
       r.since AS since, r.until AS until

MATCH (k:CourtCase)-[:INVOLVES]->(c:Company) WHERE c.id IN $company_ids
RETURN c.name AS company, k.case_no AS case_no, k.court AS court, k.nature AS nature, k.status AS status

output.algorithm: algo.betweenness on the Person-Company directorship network (both edge directions)

cypher:
CALL algo.betweenness({nodeLabels: ['Person', 'Company'], relationshipTypes: ['DIRECTOR_OF', 'HAS_DIRECTOR']})
YIELD node, score
WITH node, score WHERE node.kind = 'Person' AND score > 0
RETURN node.id AS id, node.name AS name, score
ORDER BY score DESC

MATCH (d:Person)-[r:DIRECTOR_OF]->(c:Company) WHERE d.id IN $ids
OPTIONAL MATCH (g:Group)-[:CONTROLS]->(c)
RETURN d.id AS id, collect({company_id: c.id, company: c.name, status: c.status, brand: g.name,
                             since: r.since, until: r.until}) AS boards

events.name: land_title_check
cypher:
MATCH (p:Project {id: $id})-[b:BUILT_ON]->(l:LandParcel)
OPTIONAL MATCH (l)-[po:PREVIOUSLY_OWNED_BY]->(o)
OPTIONAL MATCH (k:CourtCase)-[:INVOLVES]->(x) WHERE x = l OR x = o
RETURN p.name AS project, l.id AS land_id, l.name AS land, l.khata AS khata, l.acres AS acres,
       o.id AS owner_id, o.name AS previous_owner, o.kind AS owner_kind, po.until AS owned_until,
       collect(DISTINCT CASE WHEN k IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE
           {id: k.id, case_no: k.case_no, court: k.court, nature: k.nature, status: k.status,
            filed: k.filed, parties: k.parties, involves: x.name} END) AS cases

events.name: contractor_record
cypher:
MATCH (p:Project {id: $id})<-[:BUILDS]-(con:Contractor)
OPTIONAL MATCH (con)-[:BUILDS]->(o:Project) WHERE o <> p
OPTIONAL MATCH (k:CourtCase)-[:INVOLVES]->(con)
WITH con, collect(DISTINCT o {.id, .name, .status, .delay_months, .locality}) AS others,
     collect(DISTINCT k {.case_no, .court, .nature, .status, .filed}) AS cases
RETURN con.id AS contractor_id, con.name AS contractor, others, cases

output.investigator_report:
**Hoysala Orchid Springs (Whitefield): CAUTION. Graph risk score is 42.7, which is MEDIUM.**

**Surface view:** The project is under construction, with 3 and 4 BHK units at ₹162–290 lakh. It launched in 2024 and promises possession in 2028. It has 0 months of delay and no complaints. The BBMP plan (2023), RERA (2024) and CC (2024) approvals are all granted. The plot is A-khata.

**Hidden evidence (all of the risk comes from the contractor):**
- Hoysala Orchid Springs -> Monsoon Infra Contractors -> Chalukya Pearl Residency (26 months late).
- Monsoon Infra Contractors -> Mallige Sunrise Heights (22 months late) and Lakeshore Tranquil Bay (18 months late).
- Monsoon Infra Contractors -> C.C. 3381/2025, a cheque-bounce case in Magistrate Court, Bengaluru. It was filed in 2025 and is pending.
- Monsoon Infra Contractors' other three projects are all late, so its on-time share is 0%.

**Developer track record:** Hoysala Yelahanka Projects Pvt Ltd is active. It is linked to two sister companies, Hoysala Hennur and Hoysala Sarjapur, through shared directors. Those directors are Tejas Reddy, Swathi Joshi and Shruti Shenoy, and none has a former directorship. The group has no failed companies, no stalled projects and no court cases. Its Hoysala Heights project was delivered 3 months late, and Hoysala Haven is running 1 month late.

**Land title:** The plot is Sy. No. 36/6, Hagadur, 5.4 acres, A-khata. The previous owner, Thomas Gowda, held it until 2023. The graph shows no court cases on the land or the previous owner.

**"30-year brand" claim:** The graph records Hoysala Living as a brand since 1996, which is about 30 years. However, the developing company was incorporated only in 2022. Directorships at that company are listed from 2005 onward, which is before its incorporation date. The graph doesn't explain this, so the brand's age rests on the group, not this entity.

**Verify offline:**
- Check Monsoon Infra's delivery record and the status of the cheque-bounce case.
- Check whether the builder-buyer agreement has delay penalties and a contractor-change clause.
- Check the RERA filings. The brochure and the approvals list show different RERA numbers.
- Confirm the actual brand history.

No budget, BHK or locality preferences are recorded for this buyer, so I didn't search for alternatives.
